newsitem.title: RWANDA: Burundi refugees return home from Rwanda.
newsitem.headline: Burundi refugees return home from Rwanda.

text.p: At least 1,700 Burundian refugees left a camp in southwest Rwanda this week and returned home to northwest Burundi, the U.N. refugee agency said on Friday.
The refugees left the camp near Cyangugu and the number of those returning to Burundi could be higher, regional UNHCR spokesman Paul Stromberg said.

"Among reasons cited were that the local situation is calmer in Burundi or that the refugees have crossed back to harvest crops, possibly coffee," Stromberg said, adding the figure came from local authorities.

UNHCR maintains a policy of not helping refugees repatriate to Burundi where civilians are frequently massacred in a bitter ethnic war between the Tutsi-dominated army and insurgents of the majority Hutu ethnic group.
Most of the mainly-Hutu Burundi refugees have returned to Cibitoke province in northwest Burundi, an area severely affected by the conflict.
Local Rwandan military authorities stopped forcibly repatriating Burundian refugees from the Cyangugu area last September after an appeal by UNHCR.
Hundreds have died in Rwanda since last November in attacks by Hutu militia groups and reprisals by the Tutsi-led army. Six expatriates have also been killed this year.
At least 4,300 Burundian refugees are thought to remain in Rwanda, Stromberg said.
